overview.purpose: Simple, reliable, and efficient distributed task queue in Go backed by Redis for asynchronous job execution with at-least-once delivery semantics.
overview.architectureType: Redis-backed Client-Server task queue with distributed lease expiration, periodic heartbeater renewals, centralized sweep recoverer, and PubSub out-of-band cancellation.
keyDifferentiators: Lease-based active task tracking in a Redis sorted set (score = Unix expiration timestamp) periodically renewed by a heartbeater goroutine rather than persistent connection-bound locks
Weighted and strict priority queue scheduling using greatest-common-divisor normalization and pseudo-random queue selection
Task grouping with configurable aggregation triggers (grace period, max delay, max size) executed via atomic Lua check-and-stage scripts
Decentralized PubSub-based task cancellation allowing out-of-band context revocation across distributed worker processes
Pipeline-based batch enqueueing with Lua script preloading (EVALSHA) to eliminate NOSCRIPT failures on cold Redis instances

evidence.observation: Composes user-specified options (retries, timeouts, deadlines, uniqueness TTL, group keys, retention), marshals TaskMessage, and routes to immediate enqueue, future schedule, or aggregation group.

components.name: Server
stateManaged: Server operational lifecycle states (srvStateNew, srvStateActive, srvStateStopped, srvStateClosed)

evidence.observation: Coordinates concurrent startup and ordered graceful shutdown of forwarder, processor, recoverer, syncer, subscriber, janitor, aggregator, healthchecker, and heartbeater goroutines.

components.name: Processor
stateManaged: Task execution outcomes (succeeded, retry, archive, revoke, timeout)

evidence.observation: Acquires a concurrency token from sema channel, dequeues task via broker, creates time-bounded Lease and context, launches worker goroutine with panic recovery, and routes completion/failure.

components.role: Redis Storage Engine & Atomic Lua Execution

stateManaged: Redis Keys: pending list, active list, scheduled ZSET, retry ZSET, archived ZSET, completed ZSET, lease ZSET, task hashes (asynq:{<q>}:t:<id>), group ZSETs, server/worker metadata

evidence.observation: Atomic Lua script verifies task hash non-existence, sets task metadata hash with state 'pending', and pushes task ID to queue pending list.

components.name: Heartbeater
stateManaged: Server state snapshots in Redis (asynq:servers, asynq:workers)

evidence.observation: Iterates active workers, checks local lease validity, issues broker.ExtendLease (ZADD XX score=now+30s), resets in-memory lease deadline, and writes server/worker state with TTL.

components.name: Recoverer
stateManaged: Recovery of dead worker tasks to retry or archived queues

evidence.observation: Scans lease ZSET for scores older than now - 30 seconds (tolerating 30s clock skew) and moves expired tasks to retry or archive with ErrLeaseExpired.

components.name: Forwarder
stateManaged: Migration of due tasks from scheduled/retry ZSETs to pending list or group ZSETs

evidence.observation: Invokes broker.ForwardIfReady across configured queues, executing forwardCmd Lua script to batch-move ready tasks (score <= now) up to 100 at a time.

components.name: Subscriber
stateManaged: Redis PubSub subscription connection on asynq:cancel
Mapping of active task IDs to context.CancelFunc

evidence.observation: Maintains persistent subscription to asynq:cancel, receiving cancellation task IDs and triggering matching local context.CancelFunc instances.

components.name: Syncer
components.role: Asynchronous State Sync Buffer & Retry Queue
stateManaged: Pending sync request retry slice with expiration deadlines

evidence.observation: Buffers failed state mutations (Done, MarkAsComplete, Retry, Archive) and retries them every 5 seconds until individual request deadlines expire.

components.name: Janitor
stateManaged: Batch deletion of expired completed tasks from completed ZSET and task hashes

evidence.observation: Periodically calls broker.DeleteExpiredCompletedTasks, executing deleteExpiredCompletedTasksCmd Lua script in batches of 100.

components.name: Aggregator
stateManaged: Group check interval timer (default min(7s, gracePeriod))

evidence.observation: Executes aggregationCheckCmd Lua script, reads staged task messages, invokes user GroupAggregator function, enqueues merged task, and deletes the aggregation set.
Fires cron trigger, enqueues task via Client.Enqueue, and records enqueue event in Redis sorted set history (max 1000 events).

invariants.atomicStatement: Task dequeue atomically moves a task ID from the pending list to the active list and registers a 30-second lease score in the lease sorted set within a single Redis Lua script.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: dequeueCmd Lua script combining unpaused guard check, RPOPLPUSH, HSET state='active', HDEL pending_since, and ZADD lease (now+30s) id.

testEvidence.observation: Verifies that dequeue on populated pending list returns the task message and lease expiration timestamp exactly 30 seconds in future while mutating Redis pending, active, and lease structures atomically.

historicalContext.context: Foundational atomic dequeue primitive preventing multiple workers from popping the same task concurrently.

invariants.atomicStatement: Task uniqueness locks utilize atomic Redis SET NX EX on key asynq:{<qname>}:unique:<tasktype>:<md5> to reject duplicate task ingestion within the configured TTL window with ErrDuplicateTask.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: enqueueUniqueCmd, scheduleUniqueCmd, and addToGroupUniqueCmd Lua scripts executing SET KEYS[1] ARGV[1] NX EX ARGV[2] before task insertion.

testEvidence.observation: Asserts that calling EnqueueUnique with an identical type, payload, and queue within TTL returns ErrDuplicateTask (-1 in Lua) and does not insert second task.

historicalContext.context: De-duplication architecture preventing duplicate job insertion during network retries.

invariants.atomicStatement: recoverLeaseExpiredTasks ignores active tasks whose lease score expired less than 30 seconds ago to tolerate NTP clock drift and minor network jitter.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: recoverer.recoverLeaseExpiredTasks computes cutoff as time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Second) and passes cutoff to ListLeaseExpired (ZRANGEBYSCORE lease -inf cutoff).

testEvidence.observation: Test case 'with multiple active tasks, and one expired' asserts task with lease expired 2m ago is recovered to retry, while tasks expiring 20s in future remain untouched in active and lease sets.

historicalContext.context: 30-second buffer specifically prevents aggressive re-execution of tasks running on machines with minor time skew.

invariants.atomicStatement: Active workers periodically extend their task leases in Redis by 30 seconds using ZADD XX on the queue lease sorted set during heartbeat intervals.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: heartbeater.beat checks w.lease.IsValid() and issues broker.ExtendLease (ZAddXX lease score=now+30s), updating in-memory lease deadline.

testEvidence.observation: Verifies that ExtendLease updates sorted set score for existing task IDs by exactly LeaseDuration (30s) and ignores non-existent task IDs via XX option.

historicalContext.context: Dropped GT option from ZAddXX to ensure backward compatibility with Redis < 6.2.0.

invariants.atomicStatement: Worker pool concurrency is bounded locally by a buffered channel counting semaphore of capacity Concurrency, preventing more than Concurrency workers from executing concurrently.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: processor.exec sends token to p.sema before calling broker.Dequeue and releases token via <-p.sema upon task completion or dequeue failure.

testEvidence.observation: Asserts all tasks are processed concurrently up to configured semaphore capacity and all tokens are returned upon shutdown.

historicalContext.context: Ensures channel buffer size and semaphore token return prevent worker goroutine exhaustion.

invariants.atomicStatement: Task cancellation messages published to Redis PubSub channel asynq:cancel trigger asynchronous context cancellation for matching active task IDs on worker nodes.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: subscriber.start receives task ID string from pubsub.Channel(), queries base.Cancelations map, and calls matching context.CancelFunc.

testEvidence.observation: Asserts registered cancel function is called when matching task ID is published to asynq:cancel and ignored for non-matching IDs.

historicalContext.context: Fixed Redis connection leak on subscriber connection failure during retry loops.

invariants.atomicStatement: Failed state mutations during worker completion (Done, MarkAsComplete, Retry, Archive) are enqueued to an in-memory syncer channel and retried every 5 seconds until their lease deadline expires.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: processor handleSucceededMessage and handleFailedMessage push syncRequest structs to syncRequestCh on broker error; syncer.start retries until req.deadline.Before(now).

testEvidence.observation: Verifies that transient Redis failures during task completion are queued and retried successfully on subsequent syncer ticks.

historicalContext.context: Synchronizes worker completion state against intermittent network disconnects without blocking worker goroutines.

invariants.atomicStatement: BatchEnqueue executes independent Lua scripts inside a Redis pipeline with preloaded script hashes (EVALSHA), silently skipping existing task IDs without rolling back earlier items.
invariants.enforcingMechanism: BatchEnqueue runs enqueueCmd.Load / scheduleCmd.Load to prevent NOSCRIPT errors inside pipeline, executes pipe.Exec, and rolls back queuesPublished cache on connection error.

testEvidence.observation: Sub-scenario 'duplicate IDs skipped' asserts batch containing 3 tasks with 1 duplicate inserts exactly 2 tasks, returns count 2, and leaves existing task intact.

historicalContext.context: Fixed NOSCRIPT error on fresh Redis instances caused by pipeline Script.Run omitting EVAL fallback.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Worker GC Pause / Network Cutoff Exceeding Lease Duration + 30s Margin Causes Dual Execution
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: recoverer.recoverLeaseExpiredTasks scans asynq:{<q>}:lease for members with score <= now - 30s.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Recoverer transitions task from active to retry (or archived) queue. The stalled worker's local lease expires (l.IsValid() == false), canceling its Context. When the stalled worker attempts completion, doneCmd/markAsCompleteCmd fails with NOT FOUND.

sourceEvidence.observation: Recoverer extracts expired tasks and triggers broker.Retry or broker.Archive with ErrLeaseExpired error.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Absence of distributed lock heartbeat in crashed worker process leads to permanent task starvation in active queue without central sweeper.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Implemented central recoverer with 30s clock skew tolerance and Lease abstraction to notify local worker.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Add monotonic fencing tokens or lease generation numbers to active tasks so re-leased tasks reject state transitions from superseded workers even if re-enqueued under the same task ID.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Redis PubSub Connection Leak on Subscriber Receive Error Exhausting Connection Pool
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Subscriber retry loop failed to close redis.PubSub when Receive() encountered network error following successful Subscribe().
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Explicit pubsub.Close() invocation upon Receive() error prior to returning from CancelationPubSub().

sourceEvidence.observation: pubsub.Close() is called immediately when pubsub.Receive(ctx) returns a non-nil error.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: When redis.Subscribe succeeded but Receive() failed, pubsub connection remained unclosed, leaking one Redis socket per retry iteration.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added pubsub.Close() before returning error in CancelationPubSub (commit dd3c923f4406085d36a8efb7299202a8133e0fd5).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Ensure all network resources opened during multi-step handshakes are closed via explicit error-path teardown.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Pipeline NOSCRIPT Execution Failure on Cold Redis / SCRIPT FLUSH in BatchEnqueue
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: go-redis Script.Run on a pipeline only sends EVALSHA without the automatic EVAL fallback that non-pipelined calls possess.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Preload required Lua scripts via Script.Load(ctx, r.client) before constructing the Redis pipeline.

sourceEvidence.observation: Preloads enqueueCmd and scheduleCmd to ensure SHA digests exist in Redis script cache before executing pipeline.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: On freshly started Redis or after SCRIPT FLUSH, pipelined EVALSHA returned NOSCRIPT for all batched tasks.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added script preloading loop with Load() before pipeline command dispatch.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Always preload Lua scripts explicitly when dispatching script invocations through Redis pipelines.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Lua Arithmetic Crash on Non-Existent Key in Memory Usage Inspection Script
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: MEMORY USAGE command returns nil for expired or deleted task keys, which Lua coerces to boolean false, causing arithmetic crash (attempt to perform arithmetic on a boolean value).
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Added nil guards around all MEMORY USAGE calls and divide-by-zero checks on sample sizes in memoryUsageCmd.

sourceEvidence.observation: Checks if bytes then memory = memory + bytes end for active, pending, and scheduled task key samplings.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Deleted task keys sampled by MEMORY USAGE returned nil/false, crashing /api/queues endpoint in asynqmon.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added nil guards around MEMORY USAGE calls in Lua (commit 2fd155e31da91ecbe2d3f3f8475eee485805cd41).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Type-check and nil-guard all Redis return values inside Lua scripts before performing numerical operations.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Redis Sentinel URI Ignoring Database Number Routing Connections to Default DB 0
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: parseRedisSentinelURI ignored the /<dbnumber> URI path segment.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Extracted DB number from URI path matching standalone parseRedisURI logic.

sourceEvidence.observation: Parses path segment from redis-sentinel URI to configure target DB number in RedisClientOption.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Sentinel URIs connecting to DB other than 0 were silently routed to DB 0, corrupting or isolating task queues.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Added path parsing for DB number in parseRedisSentinelURI (commit 07898eade0b221f1475cbcc0775e7619f965fce3).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Ensure uniform URI parsing specifications across all connection schemes (standalone, sentinel, cluster).

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: BatchEnqueue Pipeline Atomicity Documentation and Script Preloading NOSCRIPT Bug Fix
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Script.Run on Redis pipelines only sends EVALSHA without EVAL fallback on NOSCRIPT, causing failure on cold Redis instances.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Preload Lua scripts before pipeline execution and document non-transactional nature (partial success possible, duplicate IDs silently skipped).

evidence.observation: Preloads enqueueCmd and scheduleCmd via Script.Load and rolls back queuesPublished cache on pipeline failure.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Redis PubSub Connection Leak on Subscriber Receive Error in CancelationPubSub
historicalEvolution.rootCause: When redis.Subscribe succeeded but Receive() failed, pubsub connection was not closed, leaking a Redis socket on each retry iteration until pool exhaustion.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Explicitly close pubsub before returning error in CancelationPubSub and added TestCancelationPubSubReceiveError test case.

evidence.observation: Calls pubsub.Close() before returning error on receive failure.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Nil Boolean Guard for MEMORY USAGE in memoryUsageCmd Lua Script
historicalEvolution.rootCause: MEMORY USAGE returned nil for deleted/expired keys, which Lua coerced to false, crashing arithmetic operations during queue stats computation in asynqmon.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added nil guards around all three MEMORY USAGE invocations and divide-by-zero checks on sample counts in Lua.

evidence.observation: Wraps bytes arithmetic in if bytes then ... end blocks in memoryUsageCmd.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Drop GT Option from RDB.ExtendLease for Redis Version Compatibility
historicalEvolution.rootCause: GT option in ZAdd requires Redis v6.2.0+, breaking compatibility with older Redis deployments (v4.0+).
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Replaced ZAddGT with standard ZAddXX in ExtendLease, trading monotonic score progression for engine compatibility.

evidence.observation: Uses ZAddXX on LeaseKey without GT qualifier.

historicalEvolution.milestoneOrBug: Task Aggregation Check Interval Alignment with Grace Period
historicalEvolution.rootCause: Aggregator only checked most recent entry against grace period; if aggregation check interval was larger than grace period, tasks could wait indefinitely.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Set aggregator polling interval to min(defaultAggregationCheckInterval, gracePeriod).

evidence.observation: Initializes interval = min(defaultAggregationCheckInterval, params.gracePeriod).

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Worker has exclusive ownership during task execution.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: If worker execution blocks for longer than lease duration (30s) + clock skew margin (30s), recoverer reassigns task to retry/archived queue. If a second worker dequeues the re-enqueued task, the original worker's completion scripts (doneCmd, markAsCompleteCmd) lack token fencing (they only check LREM active 0 <id> and ZREM lease <id> without worker ID verification). The original stalled worker can remove the task from active and delete/complete it out from under the second worker.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: doneCmd and markAsCompleteCmd execute LREM against active list matching only task ID ARGV[1]. No worker token or epoch number is verified in Redis.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: BatchEnqueue provides atomic task registration for all items in a batch.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: BatchEnqueue executes independent Lua scripts inside a Redis pipeline without MULTI/EXEC. If a task ID already exists in Redis, enqueueCmd returns 0 and skips insertion, yet BatchEnqueueContext returns Err == nil for the entire batch, masking the dropped duplicate.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: BatchEnqueueContext constructs successful TaskInfo for every item that passed local validation without verifying whether the Lua script returned 1 or 0.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: ExtendLease strictly advances lease expiration monotonically.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Due to dropping the GT flag in ExtendLease (ZAddXX without GT) for Redis 4.0+ compatibility, an out-of-order network packet or delayed heartbeat can set the lease score in Redis to an earlier timestamp, regressing the lease expiration.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: r.client.ZAddXX(context.Background(), base.LeaseKey(qname), zs...) unconditionally overwrites the score with expireAt.Unix() regardless of current score value.

boundaryConditions: Process pauses or CPU starvation exceeding 60s cause the central recoverer to re-enqueue active tasks while worker goroutines continue running, leading to dual execution on non-idempotent task handlers.
Out-of-order network delivery during lease extension can regress lease timestamps in Redis due to absence of ZADD GT in ExtendLease.
Redis Sentinel failover during pipelined BatchEnqueue can cause partial batch ingestion where only a subset of tasks reach the new master.
Global Redis keys (asynq:servers, asynq:workers, asynq:cancel) do not use hash tags, requiring single-node or specialized proxy routing in Redis Cluster environments.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes local worker system clocks and Redis server clocks remain synchronized within 30 seconds of drift; significant clock jumps invalidate lease and recovery timing.
Assumes user task handlers cooperatively respect context cancellation (ctx.Done()) upon lease expiration; non-cooperative handlers run until process termination.
Assumes in-memory queuesPublished sync.Map cache remains synchronized with Redis all-queues set across Redis flushes or cluster reconfigurations.
acceptedTradeOffs: At-least-once delivery over strict exactly-once: duplicates can occur under network partitions, worker crashes, or extended GC pauses.
Non-transactional pipeline in BatchEnqueue over MULTI/EXEC to avoid blocking Redis single-threaded execution on large batches and avoid multi-key slot constraints in clustered Redis.
Polled dequeue over blocking pop (BLPOP/BRPOPLPUSH) to enable weighted priority and random queue selection, trading increased Redis command volume for flexible priority scheduling.
Redis 4.0+ backward compatibility over monotonic lease extension (ZADD XX without GT), trading strict monotonic advancement for broad engine compatibility.
